text: Prompt caching: you think your hundred-page P D F costs you once, but without it, thirty questions actually cost you full price thirty times.
Without caching, it's a student re-reading the whole book per question.
Question one: all one hundred pages, full price.
By question thirty: paid thirty times.
With prompt caching, question one pays a quarter more, by default, to save its work.
Questions two to thirty reuse that work for about a tenth on most models, and usually answer sooner.
The document goes first, the same every time; only the new question is read fresh.
Open A I's math: ten requests cost just over two full reads, not ten.
That's how you stop paying full price thirty times.
The catch: on Claude, unused saved work can fade after five minutes, by default.
Same book: read once, reuse the work.
